{{Current events|year=2020|month=03|day=11|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]], [[Afghan peace process]]
**The [[Taliban]] rejects the [[Government of Afghanistan|government]]'s conditional prisoner release order announced by [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]]. The Taliban demand 5,000 Taliban prisoners held by the government be released before intra-Afghan dialogue can be initiated. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/03/taliban-rejects-afghan-gov-conditional-prisoner-release-order-200311073806368.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019–20 Persian Gulf crisis]], [[2020 Camp Taji attack]]
**A rocket attack on [[Camp Taji]], [[Baghdad Governorate]], housing [[Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve|coalition]] and [[Iraqi Army|Iraqi]] troops, kills two [[United States Army|Americans]] and a [[British Army|British]] service member; 12 other people are injured. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-51842744 (BBC)]  

;Business and economy
*[[Socio-economic impact of the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic]]; aftermath of [[Black Monday (2020)|Black Monday]]
**The [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] [[stock market crash|plunges]] 1,400 points and enters a [[Market trend#Bear market|bear market]]. [https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/us-stocks-march-11-2020 (Fox News)]
**The [[bond market]] falls, in the first time since the [[ financial crisis of 2007–08]] that the stock and bond markets moved in the same direction, indicating a massive sell-off of portfolios as investors seek cash. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/12/upshot/markets-weird-coronavirus.html?action=click&module=Top%20Stories&pgtype=Homepage (NY Times)]
*The world's largest annual [[video game industry]] event [[E3 2020]] is officially cancelled due to concerns over the coronavirus. The highly anticipated event was scheduled to take place on June 9, ahead of major console launches for [[Microsoft]] and [[Sony]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-51836036 (BBC)]

;Health and environment
*[[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] officially declares the outbreak as a [[pandemic]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/coronavirus-who-says-covid-19-outbreak-is-a-pandemic-1.5493411 (CBC)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Italy]]
***The [[Index case|patient zero]] in [[Italy]] has been identified as a man from [[Germany]] who arrived in the country at the end of January. [https://www.tgcom24.mediaset.it/cronaca/coronavirus-galli-paziente-0-arrivato-dalla-germania-il-25-26-gennaio_15995099-202002a.shtml (Tgcom24)]
***The death toll in Italy rises to 827, as nearly two-hundred more people were confirmed dead today, the largest daily increase in deaths since the outbreak began, while the number of confirmed cases rises to 12,462, according to [[Protezione Civile]]. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/health-pmn/italian-daily-coronavirus-deaths-jump-31-to-827 (National Post)]
***[[Juventus]] [[footballer]] [[Daniele Rugani]] has tested positive to coronavirus. [https://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/juventus/2020/03/11/news/coronavirus_positivo_rugani_dlla_juventus-251007946/ (La Repubblica)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***[[United Kingdom|British]] [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MP]] and [[Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State]] for the Health Ministry [[Nadine Dorries]] becomes the first UK MP to test positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-51827356 (BBC)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Belgium]]
***[[Belgium]] reports its first death resulting from COVID-19; a [[Government of Belgium|government]] statement said the patient was 90 years old. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/belgium-records-first-coronavirus-death (The Straits Times)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Moldova]]
***[[Moldova]] suspends all schools, universities and colleges for two weeks in order to prevent the spread of the virus. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-moldova/moldova-closes-schools-universities-to-prevent-virus-spread-idUSKBN20Y0VP (Reuters)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Indonesia]]
***[[Indonesia]] confirms its first death from COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-indonesia/indonesia-records-first-death-from-coronavirus-health-official-idUSKBN20Y0LN (Reuters)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Ukraine]]
***[[Ukraine]] bans mass gatherings and closes all schools for three weeks in response to the global coronavirus outbreak. The [[Government of Ukraine|government]] says some sporting events might still go ahead but without any spectators. [https://news.trust.org/item/20200311112458-33khz/ (Reuters)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in South America]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Argentina]]
****President [[Alberto Fernández]] issues an order saying that all people coming from hard-hit countries will have to self-quarantine for 14 days; failure to do so will be considered a crime. In addition, he analyses the possibility of banning all mass gatherings. [https://www.infobae.com/coronavirus/2020/03/11/coronavirus-sera-obligatoria-la-cuarentena-para-las-personas-que-viajaron-a-los-paises-mas-afectados-por-el-virus/ (''Infobae'' in Spanish)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Hungary]]
***[[Hungary]] declares a [[State of emergency#Hungary|state of emergency]] over the [[Coronavirus disease 2019|coronavirus]] outbreak, closing all university campuses and banning large gatherings, while anyone from Italy, China, South Korea and Iran will be refused entry into the country. Senior minister [[Gergely Gulyás]] says "These measures are unprecedented in the three decades since the fall of communism". [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-03-11/hungary-declares-state-of-emergency-shuts-universities-on-virus (Bloomberg)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Iran]]
***[[Iran]]'s [[Ministry of Health and Medical Education]] reports 958 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 and 63 more deaths, the highest number of deaths in a single 24-hour period in the country to date. All Iranians are now warned to stay indoors. Supreme Leader [[Ali Khamenei]] cancels his annual speech  marking the [[Iranian new year]] on March 20. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-iran/irans-coronavirus-death-toll-rises-to-354-ministry-idUSKBN20Y1G9 (Reuters)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Spain]]
***[[Vice President of the Congress of Deputies|Second Vice President of the Congress of Deputies]], former [[President of the Congress of Deputies|Speaker]] and former Minister [[Ana Pastor (politician)|Ana Pastor]] had tested positive for COVID-19 and becomes the highest-ranking official infected. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20200311/474090007230/ana-pastor-positivo-coronavirus.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
***Spanish [[Ministry of Culture (Spain)|Ministry of Culture]] orders in Madrid the closing of all ministry dependent centers, including the museums of [[Museo del Prado|El Prado]], [[Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía|Reina Sofía]], [[Royal Palace of Madrid|Royal Palace]], [[National Library of Spain|National Library]] and [[Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum]]. [https://elpais.com/cultura/2020-03-11/coronavirus-el-mundo-de-la-cultura-pone-en-mayo-sus-esperanzas-tras-el-aluvion-de-cancelaciones.html (''El País'')]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Sweden]]
***[[Sweden]] reports its first death from COVID-19, a person in their 70s. [https://www.svt.se/nyheter/lokalt/stockholm/en-person-har-avlidit-av-coronaviruset (''SVT Nyheter'' in Swedish)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Ireland]]
***[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports its first death from COVID-19, an elderly woman with underlying health conditions at a hospital in [[Dublin]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-northern-ireland-51838237 (BBC)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Qatar]]
***[[Qatar]] announces 238 new cases of confirmed COVID-19 cases in a single day. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/03/qatar-coronavirus-cases-jump-238-day-200311154834214.html (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in the United States]]
***[[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] gives a [[Prime time#Prime time in the context of U.S. radio/TV-revenues|prime-time]] statement about the coronavirus during which he announces a 30-day ban on travel from European countries with the exception of the United Kingdom. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/Politics/president-trump-deliver-prime-time-statement-coronavirus/story?id=69543646 (ABC News)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Arkansas]]
****[[Arkansas]] Governor [[Asa Hutchinson]] confirms the state's first presumptive case of COVID-19 in [[Pine Bluff, Arkansas|Pine Bluff]]. [https://katv.com/news/local/1st-presumptive-case-of-coronavirus-in-arkansas (KATV)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Alaska]]
****[[Alaska]] Governor [[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]] declares a state of emergency in preparation for the state's response to the coronavirus pandemic. [https://gov.alaska.gov/newsroom/2020/03/11/governor-issues-public-health-disaster-emergency-declaration-for-covid-19/ (Alaska Government)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Colorado]]
****The [[University of Colorado Boulder]]'s [[Conference on World Affairs]] and the [[Frozen Dead Guy Days]] event in [[Nederland, Colorado|Nederland]] are canceled due to coronavirus concerns. [https://www.dailycamera.com/2020/03/11/cu-boulder-cancels-conference-on-world-affairs/ (''Boulder Daily Camera'')] [https://denver.cbslocal.com/2020/03/12/coronavirus-frozen-dead-guy-days-nederland-crowds/ (KCNC-TV)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Delaware]]
****[[Delaware]] announces its first presumptive case of COVID-19 in [[New Castle County, Delaware|New Castle County]]. [https://news.delaware.gov/2020/03/11/public-health-announces-first-presumptive-positive-case-of-coronavirus-in-delaware-resident/ (''The State of Delaware News'')]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Honduras]]
***[[Honduras]] confirms its first two cases of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-honduras/honduras-confirms-its-first-two-cases-of-coronavirus-health-ministry-idUSKBN20Y1WE (Reuters)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Guyana]]
***[[Guyana]] confirms its first death from COVID-19, a woman in her 50s who recently traveled from New York. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-guyana-confirmed/update-1-guyana-confirms-first-case-of-coronavirus-in-woman-who-returned-from-us-idUSL1N2B503G (Reuters)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Bolivia]]
***The Government declares the national emergency after reporting a third case and [[Bolivian presidential election, 2020|presidential election]] rallies suspended. [https://www.telesurtv.net/news/bolivia-emergencia-nacional-por-coronavirus-20200311-0036.html (''TeleSur TV'')] [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2020-03-11/coronavirus-patient-turned-away-from-bolivian-hospitals (USNews)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Denmark]]
***[[Prime Minister of Denmark]] [[Mette Frederiksen]] orders the closing of all education centers for two weeks. [https://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-8102243/Denmark-goes-coronavirus-lockdown.html (Daily Mail)]

;Law and crime
*[[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases]]
**American film producer [[Harvey Weinstein]] is sentenced to 23 years in prison for two felony sex crimes. [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/harvey-weinstein-sentenced-23-years-prison-1283818 (''The Hollywood Reporter'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/11/nyregion/harvey-weinstein-sentencing.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Science and technology
*[[2020 in archosaur paleontology]]
**''[[Oculudentavis]] khaungraae'', the world's smallest dinosaur, is discovered by the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. [https://www.newsweek.com/world-smallest-dinosaur-trapped-amber-1491712 (Newsweek)]
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**Scientists discover [[WASP-76b]], an exotic planet that has a 100% chance of having hot liquid iron. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/ncna1156016 (NBC News)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic on sports]]
**[[Spain]]'s top [[association football]] division [[La Liga]] and [[France]]'s [[Ligue 1]] announce that all matches will be played [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] until April 15 in response to the coronavirus. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51815623 (BBC)]
**[[2019–20 Scottish Premiership]]
***[[St Mirren F.C.]] asks fans who are suffering symptoms from [[influenza]]-like symptoms or COVID-19 to not attend their upcoming game against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/amp/football/51838213 (BBC)]
** [[2020 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]], [[2020 NCAA Division I Women's Basketball Tournament]]
*** The [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] announces that all postseason tournaments in its winter season—not only the college basketball tournaments, but also its [[NCAA Bowling Championship|bowling]], [[NCAA Fencing Championships|fencing]], [[Artistic gymnastics|gymnastics]], [[College ice hockey|ice hockey]], [[NCAA Rifle Championship|rifle]], [[NCAA Skiing Championships|skiing]], [[Swimming (sport)|swimming]] & [[Diving (sport)|diving]], [[Indoor athletics|track & field]], and [[Collegiate wrestling|wrestling]] championships—will be held [[Behind closed doors (sport)|without fans in attendance]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/03/11/ncaa-tournament-attendance-coronavirus/ (The Washington Post)]
**[[2019–20 NBA season]]
***The [[NBA]] has announced that its 2019–20 season is on hiatus "until further notice" after [[Utah Jazz]] player [[Rudy Gobert]] tested a presumptive positive for COVID-19. [https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28887560/nba-suspends-season-further-notice-player-tests-positive-coronavirus (ESPN)]
**The {{Ill|2020 Japanese High School Baseball Invitational Tournament|ja|第92回選抜高等学校野球大会}} is cancelled in order to prevent players and related persons from having COVID-19. [https://mainichi.jp/koshien/articles/20200311/k00/00m/050/176000c#cxrecs_s (Mainichi Shimbun)]
<!-- All news items above this line -->}}
